clue.text: Fellow American facing criticism about page in text

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the criticism word goes around the page letter, enclosing it

parts.note: CRIT is a short informal word for criticism or a critique

explanation.surface: An American man facing criticism over a page he has written.
explanation.definitionFit: A manuscript is a handwritten or typed text, especially an author's original copy.

clue.text: Drink manufactured to bring energy up

indicators.note: with 'up', this says a letter of the word is shifted higher in this down entry
in a down clue, bringing a letter up moves it earlier in the word

parts.note: something manufactured is made
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A drink is produced to give someone a boost of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring ... up' shifts the E of MADE higher in the column, giving MEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an alcoholic drink brewed from fermented honey and water.

clue.text: College on the rise, achieving distinction

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Eton College is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A college climbing the rankings earns distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Note means distinction or eminence, as in a person of note.

clue.text: Made good the deficiencies of workers, bringing flexible fellow around

indicators.note: the flexible and fellow pieces go around the workers piece

parts.note: supple means flexible
Ted is a common man's name, standing for any fellow
men are workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: A manager makes up for staff shortages by bringing in an adaptable man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing ... around' is the container signal: the two-word outer piece wraps the staff, and 'workers' as men is a long-standing crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To supplement something is to add to it so as to make up for what it lacks.

clue.text: Foreign city embracing commercial means of communication

indicators.note: the city's name holds the commercial inside it

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, a city abroad, is often just Rio
an ad is a commercial or advertisement

explanation.surface: A city overseas takes up advertising as a way to reach people.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a medium for broadcasting and communicating by sound.

clue.text: Like member in cast to get drunk

definitions.meaning: a limb in a plaster cast is covered in plaster

explanation.surface: An actor in the cast gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' is a limb, not someone in a theatrical cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: coated in plaster, and slang for heavily intoxicated.

clue.text: Attempt seen as mad on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection is seen in a mirror, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bats is slang for mad or crazy

explanation.surface: A try that looks crazy when you think about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a stab at something means making an attempt at it.

clue.text: You notice gun being held in part of the capital

parts.note: thee is the old form of you

indicators.note: the gun sits inside the notice

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: Someone spots a gun being carried in a district of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the eastern part of London, Britain's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is a well-known district of London, the capital.

clue.text: Prohibit open spaces? Hard for tourists, this year

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
glades are open spaces in a wood
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Banning open spaces makes things difficult for visitors this year.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the country being promoted as a tourist destination in a campaign year when the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The country ran a visitor campaign, so it was the destination being promoted to holidaymakers that year.

clue.text: A new suggestion by old cleric down under

parts.note: a tip is a suggestion or hint
a dean is a senior cleric

explanation.surface: A fresh hint from a retired churchman living in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipodean describes Australia and New Zealand, the lands popularly called down under.

clue.text: Inclination for meat

explanation.surface: A liking for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lean means a slant or tilt, and also the fat-free part of meat.

clue.text: British resident unhappily admitting wickedness: indication of illegitimate child

indicators.note: the rearranged letters let the wickedness piece in
unhappily signals the letters of resident are disturbed

parts.note: sin is wickedness

explanation.surface: A British resident, sadly confessing to wrongdoing, bears a mark of bastardy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges the resident into ENDISTER, which the parse does not spell out; 'admitting' then lets the wrongdoing in after END.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a bend sinister, a diagonal band, was popularly taken as a mark of bastardy.

clue.text: Bug in room for secret observation?

definitions.text: Bug in room for secret observation?

parts.words: Bug in room for secret observation?
parts.note: reads like a hidden listening device, but describes an insect on the wall, an unseen watcher

explanation.surface: A listening device is planted to spy on people.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly on the wall is an unnoticed observer, as a housefly on a wall would be.

clue.text: Cut the allocation of curtain material?

parts.note: lace is a fabric used for curtains
a ration is an allocation

explanation.surface: Reducing someone's share of fabric for curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: A laceration is a cut or tear in the skin.

clue.text: In impassivity, review oldest sins

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, signalling the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Looking back over one's past wrongdoing without emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolidness is a calm, unemotional manner, a synonym of impassivity.

clue.text: Aircraft instrument showing change when the enemy comes in

indicators.note: the enemy piece enters the change word

parts.note: to alter is to change
time is often called the enemy, as in fighting time

explanation.surface: A cockpit gauge alters its reading as the enemy closes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is a familiar saying, so the enemy is TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An altimeter is the instrument on an aircraft that measures height.

clue.text: Two stints needed to secure a complete change of policy

indicators.note: the two stints hold the single letter between them

parts.note: a turn is a stint or spell
a bout is a stint or spell

explanation.surface: Two terms in office are needed to bring in a policy reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnabout is a complete reversal of opinion or policy.

clue.text: Old-fashioned father drinking endless tea

indicators.note: the father takes the tea inside him

parts.note: dad is father

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned dad keeps drinking tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from TEA, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated means out of date or old-fashioned.

clue.text: Old Greek? He would embrace this woman

indicators.note: the clue says HE wraps around the answer to make the Greek, so removing HE leaves her

parts.note: a Hellene is an ancient Greek
taken as written, split around the woman's name

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek man would hug this woman.
explanation.walkthrough: H and E wrapped around ELLEN give HELLENE, so taking H and E from HELLENE leaves ELLEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's name, which the clue calls this woman.

clue.text: Stars mixing in daring set

indicators.note: mixing in says the letters of the next words are blended

explanation.surface: Celebrities mingling with a bold crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Red giants are large, cool stars late in their life.

clue.text: A sad mourner in distress seeing the burial of one French author

indicators.note: one is buried inside the jumbled letters
distress here signals the letters are disturbed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A grieving mourner at the funeral of a French writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in distress' shuffles the mourner phrase into ANDREMAUROS, which the parse does not spell out; 'seeing the burial of' then sinks I among the last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: André Maurois was a twentieth-century French novelist and biographer.

clue.text: Give fresh life to Frenchman and wife

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and his wife revive something.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restore or revive, giving something new vigour.

clue.text: The man is in the West Country to find a goddess

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
in West Country dialect people say 'be' for 'is'

explanation.surface: A man in the south-west of England searches for a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England, where dialect uses 'be' for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hebe was the Greek goddess of youth, cupbearer to the gods.

clue.text: Part of serious plan for climbing mountains

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the letters read upwards
part of says the letters are taken from inside the next words

explanation.surface: A section of a serious plan for scaling peaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' picks SPLA from 'serious plan'; 'for climbing' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alps are a great European mountain range.

clue.text: Day after St Andrew's Day? About then it's got very cold

indicators.note: about here signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: St Andrew's Day is 30 November, so the day after is 1 December, written 1 DEC

explanation.surface: Around the start of December the weather turns freezing.
explanation.walkthrough: St Andrew's Day, Scotland's national day, is 30 November; 1 DEC with the 1 read as I gives IDEC to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means frozen over, so something that has got very cold.

clue.text: Now the deal could appear shabby

indicators.note: could appear says these letters may show up in another form

explanation.surface: Right now the agreement looks a bit worn.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel describes someone or something shabby and run-down, like worn shoes.

clue.text: Son trapped; it seems, in home

indicators.note: the son is placed in the trap word

parts.note: a net is what something seems to be trapped in

explanation.surface: A son appears to be stuck at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A son who is trapped has been netted, so S goes in NET.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest is a bird's home, and figuratively any snug home.

clue.text: Attendant in anxious state with a garment twisted at the front

parts.note: to be in a stew is to be in an anxious state

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the garment are turned around

parts.note: a dress is a garment

explanation.surface: A nervous flight attendant with a dress worn back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted at the front' swaps the first two letters of the garment, turning DR into RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A stewardess is a female attendant on a plane or ship.
